translation_notes: best case for the notation: the two Turtle string constants become g{...} islands written at their point of use, so Graph().parse(data=..., format='turtle') disappears entirely (12 + 3 triples, isomorphic to the parsed originals)

restructuring: the module-level `shapes_graph` / `data_graph` string constants are absorbed into the islands inside test_js_rules; each call still builds fresh graphs, exactly as the original re-parsed on each call. The six @prefix lines of the two Turtle prologues merge into one module-level set (rdf: and rdfs: were already unused in the source, kept for fidelity)

finding (ldpy parser gap): a trailing ';' before ']' in a blank-node property list is legal Turtle 1.1 but is rejected by the g{} parser ('predicat attendu'); the two occurrences of the source had to be dropped. Same RDF, but a verbatim Turtle paste does not always transpile

context shim: pySHACL is not installed (and js=True needs pyduktape2 plus a JS file from the pySHACL checkout), so context.validate is a recording double returning conforms=False -- the value the original test asserts. Identical for both sides
demo harness added identically to both representations: calls the test and exposes the two graphs handed to validate() as module-level variables, so the harness compares them by isomorphism
